item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Egypt's internet freedom 'Not Free' at 28/100 for 2023; it reported severe constraints, criminal penalties, harassment, surveillance, self-censorship, detainee 'recycling,' and abuse of activists, bloggers, and journalists in detention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 country assessment covers June 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023 and directly includes the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the governing system to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and describes authorities' practices; it does not establish his personal involvement in every cited act.","limitations":["The report is an external institutional assessment rather than a judicial finding.","The coverage period does not encompass all of calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, authorities continued 'recycling' detainees; at least one previously imprisoned person was resentenced on earlier charges in retaliation for online content. Activists, bloggers, and journalists who were arrested routinely suffered abuse and torture in detention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.9","4B.3","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Reported as a continuing practice during the 2022-2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's government, without proving a personal order by Sisi.","limitations":["The source does not identify the individual resentenced or provide a complete count.","'Routinely' is the report's characterization, not a quantified official dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Ahead of COP27, authorities arrested social-media users en masse for calls to protest and forced removal of critical online content; more than 150 people were detained and investigated by the Supreme State Security Prosecution, often under counterterrorism charges.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The event occurred in late 2022 but is included in the report's 2023 coverage period and is relevant as the governing practice entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the arrests and content removal to Egyptian authorities; it does not document Sisi's personal directive.","limitations":["The exact number of detainees was not known because of official opacity.","COP27 occurred in November 2022, before most of calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In January 2023, exiled activist Mohamed Ali received a life sentence in absentia for online mobilization connected to the 2019 protests.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"A dated event in January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The sentence was imposed by Egyptian judicial authorities; the source does not establish that Sisi personally directed it.","limitations":["The report does not provide the judgment text or assess the court's independence in this specific case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The government invested 60 billion Egyptian pounds in digital transformation and development; reported internet penetration was 72.2 percent as of October 2022, and the ICT sector grew 16.3 percent in fiscal year 2021-2022.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.2","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The indicators predate or overlap the 2023 assessment period and describe infrastructure and sector results carried into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the investment and infrastructure program to the Egyptian government under Sisi's presidency, not solely to Sisi personally.","limitations":["The figures are not full-calendar-year 2023 outcomes.","The source does not establish distributional effects or causal attribution to Sisi."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Internet prices remained relatively stable despite three currency depreciations since 2022; average monthly broadband cost was reported at $9.67, while fixed broadband cost was about 3 percent of annual per-capita income. However, access varied sharply by region, gender, wealth, and education.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The pricing assessment is current to January 2023, with access-distribution data from November 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The conditions concern government-regulated telecommunications markets under Sisi's administration; the source does not establish his personal responsibility for prices or disparities.","limitations":["Affordability and distribution figures derive from referenced external studies and historical data.","The report does not measure changes across the entire 2023 calendar year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Egyptian law gives authorities power to commandeer telecommunications networks in national-security or emergency circumstances; telecommunications infrastructure is centralized, and virtually all infrastructure belongs to state-owned Telecom Egypt, whose infrastructure ownership was placed under the Defense Ministry's National Service Projects Organization by a 2019 decree.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.9","5B.4","5B.5","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These legal and institutional arrangements remained operative during the 2023 assessment period.","ruler_attribution":"The legal and ownership framework was established by Egyptian state institutions during Sisi's rule; the source does not prove a personal decision by Sisi for each measure.","limitations":["The cited decree dates from 2019 and the telecommunications law from 2003.","The source describes formal powers and ownership, not a 2023 network shutdown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The National Telecommunication Regulatory Authority is subordinated to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology; its board is selected by the prime minister, chaired by the communications minister, and includes defense, finance, interior, national-security, presidential, and trade-union representatives. In 2022 it fined mobile providers 11.2 million Egyptian pounds and ordered 3.8 million pounds in refunds; ISPs were fined 24 million pounds for quality violations.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.4","5B.5","6B.5","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The institutional structure continued into 2023; the enforcement figures are from 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes an executive-controlled regulator within Sisi's government; it does not attribute board appointments personally to Sisi.","limitations":["The fines and refunds predate calendar year 2023.","Enforcement activity provides evidence of some regulation but not independent oversight."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Article 7 of the Information Technology Crimes Law permits the NTRA to order website blocking; 12 websites were blocked in 2022, and Al-Manassa was blocked for 72 hours after publishing criticism of mechanisms for holding the president accountable.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The blocking practices and Al-Manassa incident occurred during the report's 2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The legal power belongs to the NTRA and the blocking was carried out by authorities; the report does not prove Sisi personally ordered the blocks.","limitations":["Most cited blockings occurred in 2022.","The report does not provide a final judicial determination for each blocking."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"Ahead of COP27, at least seven released prisoners reported that the National Security Agency ordered them to remove social-media content critical of the government or face arrest; those who refused were re-arrested.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Reported during the 2022-2023 coverage period, immediately preceding the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to the National Security Agency under the Egyptian government; personal authorization by Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The account is based on reports from released prisoners and the source does not identify all individuals.","The events occurred before calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":22,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Egypt's digital legal framework permits website blocking without a judicial order on broadly defined national-security or economic grounds, imposes prison sentences and fines on service-provider personnel who fail to comply, and leaves blocked outlets' licensing and appeal prospects unclear.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The laws remained in force during the 2023 assessment period.","ruler_attribution":"The framework includes laws signed or enacted during Sisi's presidency; the report does not establish his personal role in each enforcement decision.","limitations":["The principal laws date from 2018 or earlier.","The source assesses the framework's safeguards, not a single 2023 case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":33,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"More than 150 people were detained and investigated for using social media to organize COP27 protests; authorities also detained people who organized a nonpolitical Batman-themed gathering and charged some protest-related users under terrorism and false-news provisions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The cited events occurred in 2022 but were within the report's 2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian security and prosecution authorities; personal direction by Sisi is not demonstrated.","limitations":["The report does not provide a complete official detainee list.","The events predate calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":37,"end_unit":39,"fact_summary":"Although Sisi terminated the state of emergency in October 2021, the government retained other restrictive laws and permanently codified many emergency-law provisions; 2019 constitutional amendments extended the possible duration of his rule to 2030 and expanded presidential control over the judiciary and the military's political and judicial authority.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","4B.10","8B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These constitutional and legal arrangements remained operative in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the emergency termination and constitutional amendments to President Sisi or his government.","limitations":["The constitutional amendments were adopted in 2019 and the emergency ended in 2021.","The source does not independently assess implementation of every amendment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":40,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"Egypt's anti-terrorism and cybercrime framework criminalizes a broad range of online activity: creating certain websites can carry a minimum five-year sentence, promoting extremist ideology can carry up to 10 years, and visiting a blocked website can carry up to one year; authorities also use prolonged pretrial detention and 'recycling' of defendants.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The framework and detention practice were active during the 2023 assessment period.","ruler_attribution":"The cited anti-terrorism and cybercrime laws were enacted or signed during Sisi's presidency; personal enforcement decisions are not individually attributed.","limitations":["The laws largely predate 2023.","The report does not quantify all prosecutions under each provision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":43,"end_unit":44,"fact_summary":"In April 2023, TikTok influencer Salma El-Shimy, who had 3.4 million followers, was sentenced to two years in prison and fined $3,230 for her social-media content promoting body positivity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.3","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","4B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"A dated event in April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The sentence was imposed by Egyptian authorities; the source does not establish a personal order by Sisi.","limitations":["The report does not provide the full judgment or the precise legal basis for the sentence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":44,"end_unit":45,"fact_summary":"Human-rights lawyer Mohamed el-Baqer, detained for nearly five years, was released in July 2023.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.3","7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"A dated event in July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The release was carried out by Egyptian authorities, but the source does not identify who ordered it or establish a broader policy correction.","limitations":["The source does not state whether the release was unconditional or accompanied by restrictions.","One release does not establish systemic improvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":50,"end_unit":53,"fact_summary":"Egyptian law requires SIM-card users to provide personal data, restricts encryption equipment without NTRA and security-agency consent, and reportedly enabled the COP27 app to access encrypted messages, emails, texts, and device data while requiring personal registration and location tracking.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal restrictions remained in force in 2023; the COP27 app evidence concerns late 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The restrictions and app were government measures under Sisi's administration; the source reports allegations about the app and notes official denial by Egypt's COP27 envoy.","limitations":["The app's alleged capabilities were disputed by Egyptian officials.","Some cited legal measures predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":53,"end_unit":54,"fact_summary":"The cybercrime law permits national-security agencies to access user data without judicial oversight or clear regulation, and the anti-terrorism law permits monitoring of internet traffic and social-media activity; the report says surveillance operations lack transparency.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal and institutional surveillance framework remained operative during the 2023 assessment period.","ruler_attribution":"The authorities' powers derive from laws and institutions operating under Sisi's government; personal authorization by Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The source describes legal authority and reported practice rather than a complete 2023 surveillance dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":56,"end_unit":57,"fact_summary":"The 2018 cybercrime law requires telecommunications providers to retain user data for 180 days and assist surveillance; agencies may request stored data without a judicial order. Although a data-protection law was ratified in 2020, it exempted national-security authorities, did not guarantee regulator independence, and remained suspended at the end of the coverage period for lack of executive regulations.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.9","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The data-retention regime and suspended safeguards remained relevant during the 2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The legal framework and ratified data-protection law were adopted during Sisi's presidency; the report does not attribute the missing regulations personally to him.","limitations":["The underlying laws predate 2023.","The report does not identify the cause of the missing regulations beyond their absence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, at least one social-media user was forcibly disappeared after posting a political song on TikTok; the report also states that imprisoned activists, bloggers, and journalists frequently experienced abuse and torture and that security forces operated with impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report presents the disappearance and abuse pattern as part of the 2022-2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian security and prison authorities; personal involvement by Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The source identifies at least one case but does not give a complete count.","The characterization of impunity is the report's assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2dadab5e446943b7","start_unit":64,"end_unit":65,"fact_summary":"A May 2023 Kaspersky report found that international hacking teams targeted Egyptian government institutions for espionage and data theft; the report also recorded major malware and data-compromise threats affecting Egyptian users.","question_ids":["1B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional cyberattack finding is dated May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The attacks were attributed to international hacking teams, not to Sisi or the Egyptian government; the fact concerns a risk environment during his rule.","limitations":["The source does not describe the government's defensive response or whether it corrected vulnerabilities.","The private-user incidents cited alongside the institutional attacks are not ruler-attributable."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a Freedom House internet-freedom report whose coverage period runs from June 1, 2022 to May 31, 2023, so several relevant findings precede or only partially overlap calendar year 2023.","Facts are attributed to Sisi personally only where the document expressly links an action to him; institutional conduct by Egyptian authorities is separately qualified.","No scores are assigned."]}
